questions.prompt: Why enforce "a balance can't go negative" with a CHECK constraint, rather than only in your application code?
options: The database checks numbers faster than application code
Application code can't compare numbers reliably
The constraint holds for every program that writes, including scripts, admin tools, and next year's services
Constraints make the table smaller on disk

questions.prompt: The column accounts.user_id is a foreign key referencing users.id. What does that guarantee?
options: Each user has exactly one account
Every account's user_id refers to a user that exists
Accounts are stored in user id order
Two accounts can't belong to the same user

questions.prompt: A user's email address is copied into every one of their account rows. What's the main risk?
options: The copies can disagree when the email changes
Reads of an account become slower
The foreign key from accounts to users stops working
Emails can no longer be indexed

questions.prompt: Which data fits best into a single embedded document?
options: Friendships between users of a social network
Products referenced by thousands of orders
Students and the courses each one is enrolled in
A user profile and its list of addresses, always loaded together

questions.prompt: A B-tree index has a fanout of 500 and holds about 60 billion keys. How many page reads does finding one key take?
options: About 2
About 4
About 36
About 500

questions.prompt: There's an index on (from_account, created_at). Which query can it speed up?
options: WHERE created_at > '2024-01-01'
WHERE to_account = 20
WHERE from_account = 10 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10
WHERE amount > 100

questions.prompt: Why not add an index on every column, just in case?
options: Every index slows down every write to the table and takes space
A table can only have one index
Indexes make range queries slower
Indexes go out of date and return wrong rows

questions.prompt: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for a query prints SCAN accounts. What does it mean?
options: The query found its rows with an index lookup
The results were cached
The results had to be sorted after fetching them
The database reads every row of accounts to answer it

questions.prompt: A transfer runs inside a transaction. The process crashes after debiting account 10, before crediting account 20. What does the database hold afterward?
options: Account 10 debited and account 20 unchanged
Neither write: the debit is rolled back
Both writes: the credit is replayed on restart
Whatever the application decides when it restarts

questions.prompt: What does a database do before it reports that a COMMIT succeeded, so the data survives a crash?
options: Keeps the writes in the OS page cache
Copies the writes to every replica
Writes them to the write-ahead log and calls fsync
Updates every index, then waits a second
